title: Simple Weil objects are generated by finitely many geometric simple subobjects
statement: Let $k_0$ be finite and $\ell$ an invertible prime. Let $X/k_0$ have irreducible geometric fiber, and let $V$ be an irreducible lisse source Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. There are finitely many irreducible geometric local systems $S_i$, monomorphisms $m_i:S_i\hookrightarrow\bar V$, and an epimorphism $\bigoplus_iS_i\twoheadrightarrow\bar V$ whose components are $m_i$.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: Choose a nonzero geometric simple subsheaf by minimal positive stalk rank. Its successive Frobenius translates are simple. The finite partial sums are lisse images and their bounded stalk ranks eventually stabilize. A stable sum is preserved by the Weil map; that induced map is an isomorphism by rank. The sum therefore underlies a nonzero lisse Weil subobject and equals V by simplicity. The resulting finite biproduct map is epi.

theorem IsIrreducibleLisse.exists_epi_biproduct_desc {F : WeilSheaf k₀ l X}
    (hF : F.IsIrreducibleLisse) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (S : Fin N → AdicSheaf l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber)
      (m : ∀ i, S i ⟶ F.obj.carrier), (∀ i, IsIrreducibleAdicLocalSystem (S i)) ∧
      (∀ i, Mono (m i)) ∧ Epi (biproduct.desc m)
